raw.assessment: The incumbent provides a reversible assembled product, an order-slip check and layout guidance, but reported partition errors and observed customer confusion indicate incomplete protection. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, limiting any claim that full assembly inherently prevents the eight-minute target (D2-O6). Mixed batches contained every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Overlapping widths among successful and repeated insertions also limit a width-only explanation (D2-O5). Reported errors are not an audited completeness rate; combined timing and the ten-person session cannot establish pilot success.

openings.claim: Order changes may increase selection and checking time or mistakes; an order-specific parts staging card could improve the incumbent without changing assembled delivery.
openings.delta: Separate switching overhead from layout complexity, then test a count-and-shape checklist with a verified exterior-color field.
openings.prediction: With identical layout composition, alternating orders will take longer than grouped orders, principally during selection/checking; staging will reduce that difference and observed content errors.
openings.probe: Reuse six spare-board samples across paired grouped/alternating sequences for both workers, counterbalancing sequence order. Record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, plus independently checked contents. Compare current picking with staging. Admit changes only within cost caps and available time before the fixed delivery date.
assumptions: Practice and complexity can be balanced; batch association alone is not causal.

openings.claim: Does an order-specific diagram resolve short-partition confusion when supplied components are verified correct?
openings.delta: Distinguish interpretation difficulty from missing parts and insertion difficulty.
openings.prediction: If interpretation is limiting, the tailored diagram will reduce wrong-location attempts and help requests while insertion retries at correctly identified slots persist.
openings.probe: Assign five participants to each diagram, using verified matched kits and recording first location choice, insertion retries, assistance and completion time. Reuse samples. Treat this as screening; verify final pilot thresholds separately before claiming success.
assumptions: Diagrams replace existing guidance within both cost caps.
Components, rearrangeability, ordered colors/counts, footprint, capacity and delivery date remain as stipulated.

raw.assessment: Mixed batches coincide with slow orders, but activity times are unmeasured. Reports do not establish where content errors arose. Both openings are hypotheses; screening cannot establish the 60-order targets: at least 59 complete orders, median time at most eight minutes, and at least 54 unaided arrangements.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: stage each order in a reusable board tray with component outlines and an exterior-color check before assembly, reducing omissions and selection delays.
openings.delta: Changes shared-bin picking into a visibly countable kit while retaining current components and full assembly.
openings.prediction: Against ordinary picking on matched mixed-layout sequences, staging reduces selection/checking time and audited content errors; insertion time changes little. Total time includes tray preparation and resets.
openings.probe: Reuse five sample units across both workers, counterbalance methods, and separately time selection, insertion, checking and packing. Independently audit against accepted orders. Reject if added handling cancels savings or measured setup/material costs exceed either cap.
assumptions: Order slips identify required components and colors.
Tray construction fits the initial budget and delivery schedule.
Current parts preserve footprint, capacity and dismantling.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: supply the assembled base and exterior with removable partitions packed in insertion order beside an exact ordered-layout map, enabling customers to complete insertion while reducing workshop labor.
openings.delta: Relaxes the changeable full-assembly practice; replaces the generic diagram with explicit placement of every partition, including the short one.
openings.prediction: Workshop insertion savings exceed extra kitting and diagram time without reducing unaided arrangement success; persistent short-part confusion contradicts the proposed customer benefit.
openings.probe: Use ten remaining samples and ten participants, five per current versus proposed presentation, matching layout complexity. Observe completion, errors and help requests without coaching; measure total workshop time. Treat results as screening only. Check packing retention and actual costs before changing accepted orders.
assumptions: Partial assembly meets accepted sales commitments.
Counts, colors, footprint, stationery capacity and removable joints remain unchanged.
Map and packing changes fit both cost caps and the fixed delivery date.

openings.claim: Order-specific count/shape cards or outline trays may reduce selection errors and switching overhead.
openings.discriminator: Same layout mix: grouped/alternating and ordinary/staged picking; insertion changes little.
openings.probe: Counterbalance both workers with reusable samples; time selection/insertion/checking/packing plus preparation/resets; audit counts/color. Reject handling-cancelled savings.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity/practice confounds; error origin and costs unknown.

openings.claim: An exact layout diagram may resolve short-partition confusion.
openings.discriminator: Location errors decrease while correctly located insertion retries persist.
openings.probe: Five participants per diagram, verified matched components; record location choice, retries, help and completion time.
openings.uncertainty: Interpretation, missing parts and insertion difficulty remain distinct.

openings.claim: Supply assembled base/exterior, partitions packed in insertion order and exact layout map.
openings.discriminator: Insertion savings exceed added kitting/map time without worsening unaided arrangement.
openings.fit: Uncertain: partial assembly must satisfy accepted commitments.
openings.probe: Ten samples/participants, five per presentation, matched complexity; measure total workshop time, completion/errors/help, packing retention and costs.
openings.uncertainty: Transferred labor may preserve confusion; screening only.

post_distill.decision: Screen sequentially within 15 reusable samples/ten participants. All changes require 30x20 cm footprint, unchanged capacity, removable joints, accepted counts/colors/date, initial cost <=500 and recurring increase <=0.40. Synthetic reports, combined timing and small screens establish no success: separately verify >=59/60 complete orders, median <=8 minutes and >=54/60 unaided arrangements.
